transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
Election Day is just a month from today.
There are a series of new polls suggesting Democratic candidates could hold a decided
advantage going into the midterms.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro cautions polls are not predictive, but the findings are interesting
for both House and Senate races.
We can come up with some informed reasons for what might happen.
First, we've seen the most movement in the Senate, with lots of races moving in Democrats'
direction.
And that's because of what looked to be tight races in red states.
So the Senate is within reach now for Democrats.
It was highly unlikely at the beginning of this cycle.
But it's not so far afield to say that Democrats are the clear favorites to win the House.
NPR's Domenico Montanaro reporting.
As faculty and others filled at Cornell University Plaza last night, they are calling for justice.
For a former student who has alleged in a civil lawsuit, she was gang raped in 2024
at a fraternity party at the university.
The woman alleges her complaint to Cornell campus police was not properly investigated.
One of the speakers at last night's rally was Cornell student Saya Taylor.
She says blame for the case is not just for the men who allegedly committed the rape.
Stop calling it the Cornell Senate.
It's Cornell.
The systems placed by this university and the state of New York have allowed sexual assault
culture to thrive and for rape to go unpunished.
New York Governor Kathy Hochul, an ex-officio member of Cornell University's board of trustees,
has directed the state's attorney general, Letitia James, to investigate.
A new poll out today shows Democrats have a nearly two-to-one edge over Republicans
when it comes to voter trust on health care costs.
And B.R.
Selena Simmons-Duffin has more.
The cost of health care is weighing heavily on voters' minds with the midterm elections
just one month away.
That's according to the new poll from KFF, a nonpartisan health research organization.
KFF's Ashley Kurzinger says they polled 1,300 people in mid-September.
What we are seeing is that the Democratic Party has the advantage overall among all
voters on which party voters trust to handle health care.
But they also have the advantage among independent voters, and that's a really important voting
block for midterm elections.
Kurzinger says Democrats had a 10-point advantage on health costs in April.
Now that gap has doubled.
22% of voters trust Republicans on the issue compared to 42% who trust Democrats.
Selena Simmons-Duffin, NPR News, Washington.
This year's Nobel Prize in physics has gone to Belgian physicist Francis Helzen.
The Nobel Committee says he recognized ice at the South Pole could be used to track neutrinos.
These have been seen in the distant universe as well.
This is NPR.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the United States is closely watching the case of a Russian
lab worker who died last week of the plague.
Russian officials say the 28-year-old woman died of pneumonia of an unknown origin.
Local officials describe the situation in the area around her lab as stable.
There were unconfirmed Russian media reports that several hospitals in the area were under
quarantine.
Secretary of State Rubio says Russia must share more information and that the U.S. is watching
the matter hour by hour.
Pakistan says it is moving, along with Turkey, to prepare troops for deployment to Saudi
Arabia.
This came after an emergency meeting yesterday among the leaders of the three countries in
Riyadh.
Betsy Joel's reports from Islamabad.
Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia are part of the Mecca Alliance for Defense, a mutual
defense pact that says any attack on one will be treated as an attack on all.
This is the first time the defense pact has been invoked since it was signed in August.
A joint statement shared by Pakistan's Foreign Office came after recent attacks in Saudi
Arabia by Iran-backed Houthi militants.
The statement did not say how many troops were being prepared or when they might be
deployed.
For NPR News, I'm Betsy Joel's in Islamabad.
Best-selling British author and former politician Jeffrey Archer has died at the age of 86,
according to his publisher.
Archer also spent two years in prison.
He was convicted of perjury in 2001.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Democratic candidates show decided advantage over Republicans in latest midterm election polls
Cornell University student alleges gang rape at fraternity party in 2024 not properly investigated
New poll shows Democrats have nearly two-to-one edge over Republicans on voter trust in health care costs
Belgian physicist Francis Helzen wins Nobel Prize in physics for neutrino detection research
Russian lab worker dies of plague; Secretary of State Rubio says U.S. watching situation closely
Pakistan and Turkey prepare troops for deployment to Saudi Arabia after defense pact invoked
British author and former politician Jeffrey Archer dies at age 86
